chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came while he was saying 'Talbiyah' until he entered the mosque, and he was wearing a qamis (a long shirt). A group of the companions of Abu Hanifa rushed to him and said: 'Tear your qamis and remove it from your feet, for you owe a badana (a camel) and you must perform Hajj again next year, and your Hajj is invalid.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ascended and stood at the door of the mosque, he said 'Allahu Akbar' and faced the Kaaba. The man approached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was plucking his hair and striking his face.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Be still, O Abd Allah.' When he spoke to him, and the man was non-Arabic speaking, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What do you say?'

He said: 'I was a man who worked with my hands, and savings accumulated for me, so I came to perform Hajj. I did not ask anyone about anything, but these people gave me a fatwa that I should tear my qamis and remove it from the front of my foot, and that my Hajj is invalid and that I owe a badana.'
He said to him: 'When did you put on your qamis? After you said Talbiyah or before?' He said: 'Before I said Talbiyah.'

He said: 'Then remove the camel from your neck, for there is no badana upon you and you do not have to perform Hajj again next year. Any man who acts in ignorance, there is nothing upon him. Circumambulate the House seven times, pray two rak'ahs near the Maqam of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), walk between Safa and Marwah, and shorten your hair.'
When it is the Day of Tarwiyah, perform ghusl and announce your intention for Hajj, and do as people do.'
And there is no harm in wearing the ring for the sake of the Sunnah, but it is disliked to wear it for adornment.

key_terms.قَمِيصٌ: A long shirt, a garment worn in Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing a shirt before entering Ihram for Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential dispute between the Shia Imams and the Hanafi school regarding the precise moment Ihram begins, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) ruling that wearing a shirt before the Talbiyah does not invalidate the Hajj or incur a *badana* (camel) expiation. The narrative illustrates the practical application of *jahala* (ignorance) in mitigating penalties, as the Imam guides the foreign pilgrim to complete his current rites and perform *Qada* (make-up) Hajj later, while also clarifying the etiquette of wearing a ring for Sunnah versus adornment.
